summary: Images supplied on 2026-11-12 of two marks the collection lacked: the PGE orange-outline mark (cropped from a Rapido Trains caboose announcement) and the British Columbia Railway dogwood mark. Other images supplied with them were recorded, not collected: J. F. Garden's book British Columbia Railway (cover), an embroidered British Columbia Railway patch, a stock photograph of a preserved green caboose (watermarked), a t-shirt print of the dogwood mark, and a decal sheet with the 1984–2004 BC Rail italic wordmark.

assets.label: PGE in an orange outline of the province
assets.sourceLocator: Rapido Trains’ “PGE and BC Rail Squamish Caboose” HO-scale launch announcement, as supplied
assets.notes: An orange parallelogram carrying a green outline of British Columbia, with PGE beneath in italic capitals: the railway’s mark of its later PGE years, as on the Squamish caboose No. 1857 in the same announcement.
assets.fidelityNote: A 74 × 82 pixel crop of a supplied image of a model maker’s announcement, unchanged. The maker’s drawing of the mark, not the railway’s artwork; its dates of use are not established here.

assets.label: British Columbia Railway — dogwood disc and wordmark, reversed on green
assets.sourceLocator: A supplied 300 × 180 drawing; the same mark is on the cover of J. F. Garden’s book British Columbia Railway, on an embroidered shoulder patch, and on a preserved caboose
assets.notes: A white dogwood with green leaves on a yellow disc, beside BRITISH COLUMBIA RAILWAY on three lines in a wide grotesque, white on the railway’s green: the mark of the British Columbia Railway name from 1972, before operations took the name BC Rail in 1984.
assets.fidelityNote: A supplied image, unchanged; its maker and origin are not recorded. The years are those of the name it carries, not dates of the mark’s use.
